## MCP-Reborn [![Build Status](https://github.com/Hexeption/MCP-Reborn/workflows/Java%20CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Hexeption/MCP-Reborn/actions?workflow=Java+CI)

MCP-Reborn is an MCP (Mod Coder Pack) for Minecraft. Use it to make modded clients and to read through the game's code. It's built on MCPConfig and ForgeGradle from the MinecraftForge team.

### :warning: WARNING :warning:: You **CANNOT** publish any code generated by this tool.

### Supported versions

1.13 to 26.3. Every Minecraft version has its own branch, and this one is for 26.1.2. To work on another version, switch to its branch.

### Java

| Minecraft      | JDK    |
|----------------|--------|
| 1.13 to 1.16.5 | JDK 8  |
| 1.17           | JDK 16 |
| 1.18 to 1.20.x | JDK 17 |
| 1.21 to 1.21.11 | JDK 21 |
| 26.1 and newer | JDK 25 |

Gradle has to run on that JDK as well. In IntelliJ you set it under Settings > Build, Execution, Deployment > Build Tools > Gradle > Gradle JVM.

### Setting up

1. Clone this branch, or download it as a zip, and open `build.gradle` in IntelliJ as a project. Any editor will do since it's a plain Gradle project. From a terminal, run the same tasks with `./gradlew <task>`.

2. Run the `setup` task. In IntelliJ it's in the Gradle tool window (View > Tool Windows > Gradle) under MCP.

    <img width="284" alt="373de4ebc77d5079584370dd7fbe8745" src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4052647/46925924-71b7b680-d026-11e8-9c29-e3ed2e43f810.png">

    This downloads Minecraft, decompiles it into `src/main/java` and copies the game's assets into `run/assets`. The first run takes a while.

3. Change whatever you like in `src/main/java`.

4. Run `runclient` to compile your changes and start the game. You can also use the "Minecraft" run configuration that IntelliJ picks up from the project.

### Installing into the launcher

1. Run the `installClient` task. It builds your client and puts it in the launcher's versions folder as `26.1.2-mcp`, json included.

2. Restart the launcher, go to Installations, make a new installation and pick `26.1.2-mcp` as its version.

To use a different name, pass `-PversionName=my_mod`. If your `.minecraft` folder isn't in the default place, point the task at it with `-PmcDir=/path/to/.minecraft`.

### Building a server

1. Run the `serverJar` task.

2. `build/server` now has `server.jar` and a `libraries` folder. Copy both to wherever the server will run, and keep `libraries` next to `server.jar`.

3. Start it like a vanilla server with `java -Xmx2G -jar server.jar nogui`. The first start creates `eula.txt`. Set `eula=true` in it and start the server again.

To try the server without building a jar, run `runserver`. It runs in the `runserver` folder.

### Adding OptiFine

Decompiled OptiFine sources that fit MCP-Reborn are in [Hexeption/Optifine-SRC](https://github.com/Hexeption/Optifine-SRC) and on [optifinesource.co.uk](https://optifinesource.co.uk).

1. Run `setup` on this branch first.

2. Download the OptiFine source for 26.1.2 and extract it.

3. Copy everything except the `assets` folder into `src/main/java`, replacing the files that are already there.

4. Copy the `assets` folder into `src/main/resources`. Create that folder if it doesn't exist.

5. Run `runclient`. OptiFine's options are under Video Settings.

Not every Minecraft version has an OptiFine source yet. The older ones in the repo are `.rar` archives.
